sense: straight, without turning or stopping: a direct route

terms.grammar: adjective; the adverb rēctā (viā), straight, directly
evidence: Ter. Eun. 87: cūr nōn rēctā intrōībās?
Traupman 213: volāre rēctā in Austriam, to fly directly to Austria
Traupman 204: in a straight line, per dīrēctum
terms.comment: To go straight there is rēctā īre, with viā understood (see straight on).

terms.gloss: straight, direct, in a straight line
evidence: Cic. N.D. 2.144: sī simplex et dīrēctum patēret
terms.comment: In a straight line is in dīrēctō or per dīrēctum (Varr. LL 7.15; Plin. NH 5.80; Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Quis hīc loquitur? ehem, tūne hīc erās, mī Phaedria? Quid hīc stābās? cūr nōn rēctā intrōībās?
phrases.english: Who’s that talking? Oh, it’s you, my dear Phaedria! Why were you standing out here? Why didn’t you come straight in?

phrases.latin: flexuōsum iter habet, nē quid intrāre possit, sī simplex et dīrēctum patēret
phrases.english: it has a winding passage, so that nothing can get in, as it could if the way lay open, simple and direct
